question.text: If the line segment joining <math><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>2,3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>5,7</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> subtends a right angle at <math><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> and the area of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> sq. units, then the maximum number of such points <math><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>xy</mi><mo>-</mo></math>plane are

solution.text:
PQ=32+42=5
Let, length of altitude through R is h

then 12×h×5=2

⇒h=45
Maximum possible length of altitude through R with right angle at R of ΔPQR (without the given area) is equal to 12PQ=52
Now, 45<52
So, 4 triangles are possible
